tip: Use strong action verbs to start each bullet point: Led, Developed, Implemented, Optimized, Designed, Architected, Reduced, Increased, Automated.
Quantify your impact with metrics: 'Reduced API latency by 40%' is far stronger than 'Improved performance'. Use numbers wherever possible.
Include a dedicated 'Technical Skills' section near the top of your resume. List programming languages, frameworks, databases, and tools with proficiency levels.
Keep your resume to one page for entry-level positions. Recruiters spend an average of 6-7 seconds on initial screening.
Use a clean, ATS-friendly format: avoid tables, images, headers/footers, and multi-column layouts. ATS systems often can't parse these correctly.
For ML Engineer roles, list specific model architectures (BERT, GPT, ResNet, LSTM) not just 'deep learning'. Mention frameworks: PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn.
Include a 'Projects' section with 2-3 substantial projects. For each: name, tech stack, what you built, and quantified impact or result.
Mirror keywords from the job description in your resume. If the posting says 'React.js', use 'React.js' not just 'React'. ATS systems do exact matching.
For Data Analyst roles, mention: SQL, Excel (advanced functions), Tableau/Power BI, Python (pandas, matplotlib), statistical analysis, A/B testing.
Include GitHub/portfolio links that are active and well-maintained. Recruiters will check them. Pin your best 4-6 repositories.
Use the STAR format for project descriptions: Situation, Task, Action, Result. End with a measurable result whenever possible.
For Full-Stack Developer roles, clearly separate frontend and backend skills. Mention: React/Angular/Vue, Node.js/Django/Flask, REST APIs, databases.
Add an 'Education' section with: degree, university name, graduation year, and CGPA/percentage if above 7.0/70%. Include relevant coursework.
Avoid generic objective statements like 'Seeking a challenging position'. Instead, use a 2-line professional summary highlighting your key strengths and target role.
For Backend Developer roles, emphasize: API design (REST/GraphQL), database optimization, authentication, caching, message queues, microservices.
Use consistent date formats throughout (e.g., 'Jan 2024 – Mar 2024'). List experiences in reverse chronological order.
Remove personal details that aren't relevant: date of birth, marital status, photo, father's name. These aren't expected in modern resumes and waste space.
Include certifications only if they're relevant and recognized: AWS Certified, Google Cloud Professional, Coursera specializations with verified certificates.
For competitive programming achievements, mention: platform ratings (Codeforces, LeetCode), contest rankings, number of problems solved. These are strong signals for DSA skills.
Use standard section headings that ATS systems recognize: 'Experience', 'Education', 'Skills', 'Projects', 'Certifications'. Avoid creative names like 'My Journey'.
Tailor your resume for each application. A resume targeting a Data Scientist role should emphasize different projects than one targeting Frontend Developer.
If you have internship experience, list it under 'Experience' with detailed bullet points. Even short internships with impact metrics are valuable.
Proofread for spelling and grammar errors. A single typo can cause rejection — use tools like Grammarly for a final check.
Save your resume as a PDF to preserve formatting across devices. Name the file professionally: 'FirstName_LastName_Resume.pdf'.
For Frontend Developer roles, mention responsive design, accessibility (WCAG), performance optimization (Lighthouse score), and cross-browser compatibility.
Include relevant soft skills demonstrated through experiences, not listed as buzzwords. Show 'Led a team of 5' instead of listing 'leadership' as a skill.
If you contributed to open source projects, highlight this prominently. Mention the project name, your contribution, and its impact (PRs merged, issues resolved).
For your strongest project, include a 'deployed at' link or demo URL. A live, working project is worth more than a description.
Use a professional email address (firstname.lastname@gmail.com). Avoid nicknames or numbers that look unprofessional.
Add your LinkedIn profile URL (customized, not the default long URL). Ensure your LinkedIn matches your resume content.
